```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false

# ---- Packages ---------------------------------------------------------------
# Loaded once here so that the analytical sections below contain only
# analytical code. Versions are reported in the reproducibility appendix.
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(sf)                 # vector geospatial data and CRS handling
  library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(purrr); library(stringr)
  library(lubridate)
  library(ggplot2); library(patchwork); library(scales); library(forcats)
  library(ggrepel)
  library(spdep)              # neighbours, weights, Moran's I
  library(sfdep)              # spacetime cube, local statistics, EHSA
  library(Kendall)            # Mann-Kendall trend test
  library(gt)                 # tables
})

source("R/utils.R")
source("R/ehsa.R")

sf::sf_use_s2(FALSE)   # planar predicates: everything is in the projected CRS
set.seed(1234)

# ---- Load the prepared objects ---------------------------------------------
# Built by scripts/01_boundaries.R .. scripts/05_markov.R. None of them holds an
# individual ACLED event: the licence does not allow event records to be
# republished, so the report reads township-level aggregates only.
DER     <- "data/derived"
bnd     <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "bnd_report.rds"))
audit   <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "acled_audit.rds"))
ts_all  <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "township.rds"))
ts_an   <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "township_an.rds"))
ts_tot  <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "ts_tot.rds"))
state   <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "state.rds"))
nation  <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "nation.rds"))
nb_an   <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "nb_an.rds"))
nb_knn6 <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "nb_knn6.rds"))
panel_q <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "panel_q.rds"))
panel_m <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "panel_m.rds"))
panel_y <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "panel_y.rds"))
LM      <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "lmsa.rds"))
EH      <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "ehsa.rds"))
MK      <- readRDS(file.path(DER, "markov.rds"))

# ---- Labels and quantities used repeatedly in the prose ---------------------
VARS <- LM$vars
VAR_SHORT <- c(conflict = "All conflict", battles = "Battles",
               erv = "Explosions / remote violence",
               vac = "Violence against civilians", fatalities = "Fatalities")
VAR_ZH <- c(conflict = "全部冲突事件", battles = "战斗", erv = "爆炸 / 远程暴力",
            vac = "针对平民的暴力", fatalities = "报告死亡人数")
# Panel titles for the five-map rows, where the full labels do not fit.
VAR_TINY <- c(conflict = "All conflict", battles = "Battles",
              erv = "Remote violence", vac = "Violence vs civilians",
              fatalities = "Fatalities")

N_TS    <- nrow(ts_an)
N_Q     <- EH$cube_info$n_times
N_EV    <- audit$loc_flow$analysed
N_FATAL <- audit$loc_flow$fatal_analysed
q_lab   <- function(d) paste0(year(d), " Q", quarter(d))

# State labels: MIMU writes the two halves of Bago and the three of Shan as
# separate states, which is how they are mapped and described.
state_pts <- state |>
  mutate(pt = st_point_on_surface(geometry)) |>
  st_drop_geometry() |>
  mutate(x = st_coordinates(pt)[, 1], y = st_coordinates(pt)[, 2]) |>
  select(ST, x, y)

# The analytical frame with every variable attached, for mapping.
ts_map <- ts_tot

# One base layer for every map: the excluded island township in hatched grey,
# the analytical townships, and state outlines on top.
map_base <- function(fill_layer, title = NULL, subtitle = NULL, legend = TRUE,
                     state_lw = 0.32) {
  ggplot() +
    geom_sf(data = ts_all |> filter(!TS_PCODE %in% ts_an$TS_PCODE),
            fill = "#e7e5e4", colour = NA) +
    fill_layer +
    geom_sf(data = state, fill = NA, colour = "#44403c", linewidth = state_lw) +
    coord_sf(datum = NA, expand = FALSE) +
    labs(title = title, subtitle = subtitle) +
    theme_map(10) +
    { if (!legend) theme(legend.position = "none") }
}
```

## <span class="en">Abstract</span><span class="zh">摘要</span> {#sec-abstract .unnumbered}

::: {.en}
Myanmar's military seized power on 1 February 2021, and the protests that
followed turned within months into a nationwide armed conflict. This report
analyses `r n_fmt(N_EV)` armed-conflict events recorded by ACLED between
January 2021 and September 2025 (battles, explosions and remote violence, and
violence against civilians), aggregated to `r N_TS` townships of the MIMU v9.4
boundaries and to `r N_Q` quarters.

Local Moran's I and Getis-Ord Gi\* locate one dominant cluster of high
conflict, the Dry Zone where Sagaing, Magway and Mandalay meet, a second belt
along the south-east from Kayin through Mon to Tanintharyi, and a broad cold
zone over the Ayeyarwady delta, Yangon and the eastern Shan hills. Violence
against civilians is confined almost entirely to the Dry Zone; explosions and
remote violence also light up the south-east. No township is a significant
high-low outlier over the whole period: violence does not appear as an
isolated island in a calm region. Year by year, the Dry Zone cluster held
through 2023 and then thinned out; by 2025 the High-High townships were split
between the Kayin border, the uplands where Mandalay meets northern Shan, and
a remnant of the old core.

The emerging hot spot analysis is where the methodological work of the report
lies. Applied as distributed, `emerging_hotspot_analysis()` in **sfdep** gives
each township's result to another township whenever the geometry is not
sorted by location identifier; its permutation null draws neighbours from
every quarter of the cube, so that a national trend is read as local
significance; and one of its class rules ignores the sign of Gi\*. All three
defects are demonstrated on these data and corrected. With a
period-conditional null the oscillating hot spots of the uncorrected output
fall from `r sum(EH$cls_compare$sfdep == "Oscillating hot spot")` to
`r sum(EH$cls_compare$pc == "Oscillating hot spot")`, and the classification
shows a chronic core in the Dry Zone, new hot spots on its southern and
eastern edges, and cold spots in the eastern Shan hills and, since 2022, in
Yangon. A null simulation shows that the commonest class, the sporadic hot
spot, is barely more frequent than chance would make it, so townships are
read by how many quarters they spent hot rather than by label alone.

A spatial Markov chain, offered as value-added analysis, shows that a quiet
township is about twice as likely to see conflict the next quarter when its
neighbours are in intense conflict, and the effect survives township and
quarter fixed effects. The *first* onset of sustained conflict, by contrast,
is no more clustered than random timing would produce: the 2021 uprising broke
out nationwide at once, and contagion governs escalation afterwards.
:::

::: {.zh}
2021 年 2 月 1 日,缅甸军方夺取政权,随后的抗议在数月之内演变为全国性的武装冲突。
本报告分析 ACLED 在 2021 年 1 月至 2025 年 9 月间记录的 `r n_fmt(N_EV)` 起武装冲突
事件(战斗、爆炸与远程暴力、针对平民的暴力),将其汇总到 MIMU v9.4 边界的
`r N_TS` 个镇区和 `r N_Q` 个季度。

局部 Moran's I 与 Getis-Ord Gi\* 识别出一个占主导的高冲突聚集区,即实皆、马圭与
曼德勒交界的**干燥带**;第二条聚集带沿东南方向从克伦经孟邦延伸到德林达依;
伊洛瓦底三角洲、仰光和掸邦东部山地则构成大片冷区。针对平民的暴力几乎完全局限
在干燥带;爆炸与远程暴力则在东南方向同样显著。就整个研究期而言,没有任何镇区是
显著的高-低异常值:暴力并不以「平静区域中孤立的岛」的形式出现。逐年来看,干燥带
聚集在 2023 年之前保持稳定,此后逐渐稀疏;到 2025 年,「高-高」镇区分散在克伦边境、
曼德勒–掸邦北部交界山地,以及老核心的残余三处。

新兴热点分析是本报告方法工作的重心。按原样使用 **sfdep** 的
`emerging_hotspot_analysis()` 时,只要几何对象没有按地点编号排序,每个镇区的结果
就会被贴到另一个镇区上;它的置换零模型从整个立方体的**所有季度**中抽取邻居,于是
全国性的趋势被误读为局部显著性;它的一条分类规则还忽略了 Gi\* 的符号。本报告用这批
数据证明并修正了这三个缺陷。改用**按期条件化**的零模型之后,未修正输出中的振荡热点
从 `r sum(EH$cls_compare$sfdep == "Oscillating hot spot")` 个降到
`r sum(EH$cls_compare$pc == "Oscillating hot spot")` 个,分类结果呈现出干燥带的长期
核心、其南缘与东缘的新热点,以及掸邦东部山地与(2022 年以来)仰光的冷点。零模型模拟
表明,最常见的类别「零星热点」只比偶然所能产生的略多,因此本研究依据镇区处于热点
状态的季度数,而不只是标签来解读。

作为附加价值分析的空间马尔可夫链表明:当邻居处于高强度冲突时,一个平静镇区在
下一季度出现冲突的概率约为原来的两倍,且这一效应在控制镇区与季度固定效应后依然
存在。相比之下,持续冲突的**首次**爆发并不比随机时间分配更聚集:2021 年的起义是
全国同时爆发的,传染机制支配的是此后的升级。
:::
